Sasha: FYI noticed a regression after yesterday's kernel-routing change. INT8 tail latency for small chat requests jumped ~2x when KV cache is cold. Profiling attached (nsys sampled run).

Anita: Oof, any traces? can you paste the nsys cmd you used? :eyes:

Sasha: Ran sampled nsys to keep file small: ```nsys profile --sampled-interval=5us -o sampled_run --trace=cuda python -m run_infer --model rwd-int8 --batch 1 --warmup 50 --requests 500```
I then filtered by kernel name and timeline. Key snippet: 
```
Kernel                                          Calls   Total(ms)  Avg(ms)
matmul_int8_kernel                              5       0.55       0.11
dequantize_host_copy                            5       0.35       0.07
matmul_fp8_fallback                              2      0.84       0.42
kv_prefetch                                        5     0.20       0.04
```
Looks like when KV miss rate spikes, runtime picks a fallback FP8 path for a couple of layers (matmul_fp8_fallback) which is slower than steady INT8 path because of extra host dequant/copy.

Marc: Huh. So kernel selection policy is choosing matmul_fp8_fallback on mismatch of quant metadata? Could be our kernel matcher failing for some sequence lengths — it falls back to a generic FP8 kernel that does host-side dequant. :thinking:

Daniel: Do we have the scheduler logs that show the decision? infra-bot, can you pull last rollout config for kernel-router?

infra-bot: deploy 2026-03-14T21:13:02 by @marc applied: kernel-router v2.1.4 (heuristic: prefer specialized kernels if static shape exact-match, else fallback to generic)

Anita: Two quick repros to run: 1) cold KV path (force cache miss) with batch=1; 2) warm KV (cache hit) same load. Compare kernel timelines and memcpy times. If dequantize_host_copy grows with cold path, that's our culprit.

Sasha: Did both: cold KV shows dequantize_host_copy = ~35% of request time, warm KV down to ~8%. When cold, we also see extra memcpy to host pinned buffer before the fallback kernel. Example trace notes: "host->device memcpy: 0.22ms" repeated.

Marc: Can you also check the kernel selector thresholds? Might be we tuned shape-match too aggressively to avoid kernel-compilation stubs, causing false negatives. If selector uses cumulative_seq_len heuristic, small variance may flip choice.

Sasha: Poked selector code, found an explicit guard: if (seq_len_variance > 0.15f) choose_generic(). That threshold was lowered in v2.1.4. Rolling back to 0.25 might reduce fallback churn.

Daniel: Tradeoff: raising threshold may pick specialized kernel for slightly varying shapes (good perf) but could degrade accuracy if quant params mismatch? Any eval data?

Sasha: Quick eval: INT8 specialized path vs fallback FP8 with host dequant: FP8 path has ~0.6% lower exact-match on our regression prompt set but latency penalty is big on cold KV (2x). For most real-time use cases, prefer latency.

Anita: Sounds like we need a two-pronged fix: 1) immediate rollback/adjust selector threshold to reduce fallbacks; 2) longer-term: move dequant to device-side for the generic kernel to avoid host memcpy penalty.

Marc: Agreed. I've opened a small PR to revert the threshold bump: https://git.redwood.ai/rwd/runtime/pull/482 (canary patch). Can we run canary on a host with heavy cold-KV sim? @Sasha please run sampled nsys and upload traces to perf bucket.

Sasha: Will run canary now on perf-canary-5, uploading traces (small). Attaching short timeline excerpt in case folks want to triage before full traces: 
```
Timeline (cold KV):
  request recv
  kv_lookup (miss)
  kv_prefetch -> device memcpy 0.20ms
  kernel_selector -> generic_fp8 (host_dequant)
  host_dequant + host->device memcpy 0.22ms
  matmul_fp8_fallback 0.42ms
  postprocess
```

Marc: Nice. If host_dequant is unavoidable for now, could we overlap memcpy with next batch's kv_prefetch? Longer-term overlap scheduling might hide cost.

Daniel: Also add a perf regression alert tied to sampled runs for canaries. If tail latency > 1.6x baseline on cold-KV, block rollout.

Sasha: noted. I'll upload traces, run warm/cold sims, and drop a short summary here when done. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
